source: Team field research at Civil Hospital Karachi (backend/data/story.json). Sticky text is the original wording; Urdu/Sindhi group titles are drafts awaiting native review.

title.ur: آرام کرنے کے لیے کوئی محفوظ جگہ نہیں
title.sd: آرام ڪرڻ لاءِ ڪا به محفوظ جاءِ ناهي

insight.en: Families stay close to the patient out of care, but the hospital has no place for them, so they are moved on.
insight.ur: خاندان دیکھ بھال کی وجہ سے مریض کے قریب رہتے ہیں، لیکن ہسپتال میں ان کے لیے کوئی جگہ نہیں ہے، اس لیے انہیں وہاں سے ہٹا دیا جاتا ہے۔
insight.sd: خاندان سارسنڀال جي ڪري مريض جي ويجهو رهن ٿا، پر اسپتال ۾ انهن لاءِ ڪا جاءِ ناهي، ان ڪري کين اتان هٽايو وڃي ٿو.

insight.en: The hospital is hard to navigate, and one wrong turn costs time a sick patient may not have.
insight.ur: ہسپتال میں راستہ تلاش کرنا مشکل ہے، اور ایک غلط موڑ سے وہ وقت ضائع ہو سکتا ہے جو ایک بیمار مریض کے پاس شاید نہ ہو۔
insight.sd: اسپتال ۾ رستو ڳولڻ ڏکيو آهي، ۽ هڪ غلط موڙ اهڙو وقت ضايع ڪري ٿو جيڪو بيمار مريض وٽ شايد نه هجي.

insight.en: Families are present but poorly informed, so they cannot make good decisions at the hospital or at home.
insight.ur: خاندان موجود ہیں لیکن انہیں بہت کم معلومات دی جاتی ہیں، اس لیے وہ ہسپتال میں یا گھر پر اچھے فیصلے نہیں کر سکتے۔
insight.sd: خاندان موجود آهن پر کين تمام گهٽ ڄاڻ ڏني وڃي ٿي، ان ڪري هو اسپتال ۾ يا گهر ۾ سٺا فيصلا نٿا ڪري سگهن.

insight.en: Treatment at Civil Hospital may be free, but staying for it is not.
insight.ur: سول ہسپتال میں علاج مفت ہو سکتا ہے، لیکن وہاں قیام مفت نہیں ہے۔
insight.sd: سول اسپتال ۾ علاج مفت ٿي سگهي ٿو، پر اتي رهڻ مفت ناهي.

insight.en: Staff care about patients, but the system around them gives them too little to work with.
insight.ur: عملہ مریضوں کا خیال رکھتا ہے، لیکن ان کے ارد گرد کا نظام انہیں کام کرنے کے لیے بہت کم وسائل دیتا ہے۔
insight.sd: عملو مريضن جو خيال رکي ٿو، پر سندن آس پاس جو نظام کين ڪم ڪرڻ لاءِ تمام گهٽ وسيلا ڏئي ٿو.

stickies.text: Sat on the footpath; told to move elsewhere with no direction given.
"Jahan baithte hain, wahan se utha dete hain." (paraphrased)
Family of four sleeps on a bedsheet on the floor outside the ward for a month.
Open-air sleeping in the heat gives little, broken sleep.
Attendants have no accommodation, so they sleep on streets or floors outside the wards.
Confused and helpless: does not know where to go or who to ask.
Asked many people for the department; one said emergency no. 3, others sent him elsewhere.
"Koi kahin aur bhej deta hai." (paraphrased)
Hours lost searching while his 7-year-old son's condition got worse.
Spent 3-4 days in a Mirpur hospital with no improvement before referral to Karachi.
Patients reach Civil Hospital with little early guidance on where to go.
Only the mother may go inside, briefly; the father waits outside with no news.
"Humein pata hi nahi wo kaisa hai." (paraphrased)
Mother cannot follow medical language, so the father gets incomplete information.
Next visit date was 10 days away; family took patient home, he worsened and was readmitted.
Wants discharge and follow-up instructions he can understand.
Patients given a 10-day follow-up date cannot afford to wait in Karachi, so treatment stays incomplete.
Tests are done but lab reports are still pending after weeks, slowing treatment.
Each trip from Thatta costs Rs 800 by bus; two brothers stay in turns.
Two brothers lose work days to stay at the hospital.
Daily food costs drain the family; the eldest brother at home pays.
Farm work has stopped, so income is lost while brothers are at the hospital.
"Roz ka khana aur rehne ka intezaam bohat mushkil hai." (paraphrased)
Extreme poverty: patients lack proper food, clean water and medicines the hospital does not supply.
Each child arrives with 6-9 attendants, crowding the emergency.
Attendants refuse to go to the pharmacy and want medicines given in the emergency.
Pharmacy is not digitised and does not always stock medicines, so prescriptions go unfilled.
Irregular shift timings with no check and balance from authorities.
Frustrated by the lack of accountability in the administration.
More intern nurses than doctors and nurses; sometimes a patient needs a doctor but only an intern is there.
About 6 people crowd around each patient, with few resources in the emergency.
Works unpaid as an intern and takes a part-time paid job at another hospital.
Too many patients per doctor plus admin delays push response times beyond acceptable limits.
Patients arrive in dirty clothes, making infection control hard.

selected.text: How might we help first-time visitors reach the right department the first time?
